url: /docs/k3sctl.md
description: >-
  Declarative lifecycle management for K3s clusters over SSH — install, upgrade,

# k3sctl

`k3sctl` is a declarative lifecycle management tool for
[K3s](https://k3s.io) clusters, created and inspired by
[k0sctl](https://github.com/k0sproject/k0sctl). Point it at a YAML file
describing your hosts and it installs, upgrades, reconfigures, backs up, and
resets the cluster over SSH.

```sh
k3sctl init --name demo --address 10.0.0.1 --agent --agent-address 10.0.0.2 > k3sctl.yaml
$EDITOR k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl apply --config k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl kubeconfig > kubeconfig.yaml
```

## What it does

* Declarative cluster configuration with servers and agents in one file.
* Installs and upgrades K3s binaries from GitHub releases, a URL, a local file,
  or an existing installation on the host.
* Generates server and agent configuration plus systemd units.
* Supports labels, taints, extra install flags, environment variables, and
  arbitrary file uploads.
* Applies additional Kubernetes manifests bundled in the configuration file.
* Automated etcd snapshots with S3 upload, retention, and pruning, plus etcd
  member validation and restore from a snapshot.
* Fetches a ready-to-use admin kubeconfig.
* Idempotent `apply`: safe to re-run, and only changes what drifted.
* Rolling upgrades with drain and cordon for both servers and agents.
* Configuration validation (`config validate`) and diff (`config diff`).
* Air-gap install: upload pre-downloaded image bundles for offline clusters.
* Dry-run mode with `--dry-run`.
* Private registry mirrors and authentication (`registries`).
* Secrets encryption at rest with key rotation and re-encryption
  (`secretsEncrypt`).
* Certificate Authority rotation (`certRotate.rotateCA`).
* Cluster join token rotation (`token.rotate`).
* Post-apply cluster health verification (`healthCheck`).
* Pre-flight checks for cgroups, kernel modules, ports, and disk (`preflight`).
* Declarative networking: cluster/service CIDRs, DNS, flannel backend,
  egress selector mode, NodePort range, and ServiceLB namespace (`network`).
* Component disabling: turn off packaged components like traefik, servicelb,
  metrics-server, and individual subsystems like kube-proxy or the Helm
  controller (`disable`).
* TLS SAN management: add Subject Alternative Names to the API server
  certificate (`tls`).
* Kubeconfig output control: file mode, group, and cluster name (`kubeconfig`).
* External datastore: MySQL, PostgreSQL, or etcd endpoint with TLS
  (`datastore`).
* API server listener: advertise address/port, bind address, HTTPS port
  (`server`).
* Security hardening: SELinux, kernel defaults protection, and encryption
  provider selection (`security`).
* Typed component arguments: pass arguments directly to kube-apiserver,
  kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, etcd, and others
  (`componentArgs`).
* Container runtime: system default registry, pause image, snapshotter,
  default runtime override, and custom resolv.conf (`runtime`).
* Embedded container registry: enable the K3s built-in Spegel distributed
  registry (`embeddedRegistry`).
* Image credential provider: external kubelet credential plugin for pulling
  images from private registries (`imageCredentialProvider`).
* Per-host node networking: external IPs, internal/external DNS names for
  multi-homed and cloud nodes (`nodeExternalIP`, `nodeInternalDNS`,
  `nodeExternalDNS`).
* Local storage: custom path for the built-in local-path provisioner
  (`localStorage`).
* Advanced etcd tuning: expose metrics, disable automatic snapshots, snapshot
  naming, and reconcile interval (`etcdAdvanced`).
* Advanced flannel options: interface selection, custom flannel and CNI
  configuration file paths (`network.flannelIface`, `flannelConf`,
  `flannelCNIConf`).
* Advanced S3 snapshot storage: session tokens, bucket lookup type, proxy,
  config secret, timeout, and per-S3 retention (`etcdSnapshots.s3`).

::: warning
Linux hosts only. `k3sctl` drives the cluster over SSH, so each host must be
reachable and must provide `sudo` or a root login.
:::

## How it works

1. `k3sctl` reads the `Cluster` document from your config file.
2. It connects to each host over SSH and detects the OS and architecture.
3. It uploads or downloads the requested K3s version, writes the server or agent
   configuration and the systemd unit, then starts K3s.
4. Once the API server answers, it applies any additional manifests found in the
   same file with `kubectl apply`.
5. `k3sctl kubeconfig` reads the admin kubeconfig back so you can use it
   locally.

Because the desired state is the file, re-running `apply` after editing it is
the normal way to change a cluster.

## Requirements

* Linux hosts for servers and agents.
* SSH access, with a key or the agent available to `k3sctl`.
* Root or passwordless `sudo` on each host.

* [Installation](./installation.md): release binary, `go install`, or build from
  source.
* [Configuration](./configuration.md): every host, K3s, and drain option.
* [Commands](./commands.md): the full CLI and the flags accepted by `apply`.

# Installation

`k3sctl` ships as a single static binary. Pick the method that fits your
workflow.

## Release binary

Download the binary for your platform and put it on your `PATH`:

```sh
curl -sSfL -o k3sctl \
  https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/k3sctl/releases/latest/download/k3sctl_$(uname -s | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')_$(uname -m)
chmod +x k3sctl
sudo install -m 755 k3sctl /usr/local/bin/k3sctl
```

Release assets are published for Linux and macOS on `amd64`, `arm64`, and
`arm`.

## With Go

If you already have a Go toolchain:

```sh
go install github.com/vinaycharlie01/k3sctl@latest
```

This installs `k3sctl` into `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`.

## Build from source

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/k3sctl.git
cd k3sctl
go build -o k3sctl .
./k3sctl version
```

## Verify the installation

```sh
k3sctl version
k3sctl --help
```

## Shell completion

`k3sctl` can print a completion script for your shell:

```sh
# Bash
source <(k3sctl completion bash)

# Zsh
k3sctl completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_k3sctl"
```

Run `k3sctl completion --help` for the shells your build supports.

## Next steps

Generate a starter configuration, edit it, and apply it:

```sh
k3sctl init --name demo --address 10.0.0.1 --agent --agent-address 10.0.0.2 > k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl apply --config k3sctl.yaml
```

See [Configuration](./configuration.md) for the full file reference and
[Commands](./commands.md) for every subcommand.

# Configuration

A `k3sctl` configuration is a single `Cluster` document with
`apiVersion: k3sctl.k3sproject.io/v1beta1`.

```yaml
apiVersion: k3sctl.k3sproject.io/v1beta1
kind: Cluster
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:
  hosts:
    - role: server
      ssh:
        address: 10.0.0.1
        user: root
        port: 22
        keyPath: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
      privateAddress: 10.0.0.1        # advertises this IP to the cluster
      installFlags:
        - --disable=traefik
      labels:
        node-role.example.com/edge: "true"
      taints:
        - dedicated=edge:NoSchedule
      environment:
        ETCD_UNSUPPORTED_ARCH: arm     # rendered into the systemd unit
      files:
        - src: ./configs/registries.yaml
          dst: /etc/rancher/k3s/registries.yaml
          perm: "0600"
      hooks:
        apply:
          before:
            - echo preparing
          after:
            - echo done

    - role: agent
      ssh:
        address: 10.0.0.2
        user: root
        port: 22
        keyPath: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
      nodeExternalIP:                    # per-host external IPs
        - 203.0.113.10
      nodeInternalDNS:                   # per-host internal DNS names
        - agent1.internal.example.com
      nodeExternalDNS:                   # per-host external DNS names
        - agent1.example.com

  k3s:
    version: v1.30.0+k3s1
    config:                            # merged into config.yaml on every host
      write-kubeconfig-mode: "0644"
      disable:
        - servicelb
    extraArgs:
      - --kubelet-arg=eviction-hard=memory.available<100Mi

    etcdSnapshots:                     # automated etcd snapshot scheduling
      scheduled: true
      scheduleCron: "0 */12 * * *"
      retention: 5
      dir: /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/db/snapshots
      compress: true
      s3:
        enabled: true
        endpoint: s3.amazonaws.com
        bucket: my-k3s-backups
        region: us-east-1
        folder: snapshots
        accessKey: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
        secretKey: wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG/bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY
        sessionToken: FwoGZXIv...          # STS session token
        bucketLookupType: auto             # auto, dns, or path
        proxy: http://proxy.example.com:8080
        configSecret: my-s3-secret
        timeout: 30s
        retention: 10                      # per-S3 retention override
      prune:                           # prune old snapshots on apply
        enabled: true
        retention: 10
        name: on-demand

    secretsEncrypt:                    # secrets encryption at rest
      enabled: true
      rotateKeys: true                 # dynamically rotate encryption keys
      reencrypt: true                  # re-encrypt all secrets with new keys

    certRotate:                        # certificate rotation on apply
      enabled: true
      rotateCA: true                   # rotate the root CA (full cluster restart)

    token:                             # cluster tokens
      serverToken: my-server-secret
      agentToken: my-agent-secret
      rotate: true                     # rotate token and restart all nodes

    registries:                        # private registry configuration
      mirrors:
        docker.io:
          endpoint:
            - https://registry.example.com
      configs:
        registry.example.com:
          auth:
            username: myuser
            password: mypass
          tls:
            caFile: /path/to/ca.pem
            insecureSkipVerify: false

    healthCheck:                       # post-apply health verification
      enabled: true
      timeout: 120s

    preflight:                         # pre-flight checks before apply
      enabled: true
      checkCgroups: true
      checkModules: true
      checkPorts: true
      checkDisk: true
      minDiskGB: 10

    airgap:                            # air-gap (offline) installation
      enabled: true
      imageBundle: /path/to/k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst

    network:                           # cluster networking
      clusterCIDR:
        - 10.42.0.0/16
      serviceCIDR:
        - 10.43.0.0/16
      clusterDNS:
        - 10.43.0.10
      clusterDomain: cluster.local
      nodePortRange: "30000-32767"
      flannelBackend: vxlan             # none, vxlan, host-gw, wireguard-native
      flannelIPv6Masq: false
      flannelExternalIP: false
      flannelIface: eth1                # network interface for flannel
      flannelConf: /etc/flannel.json    # custom flannel config file
      flannelCNIConf: /etc/cni/net.d/10-flannel.conflist
      egressSelectorMode: agent         # agent, cluster, pod, disabled
      serviceLBNamespace: kube-system

    disable:                           # disable packaged components
      components:
        - traefik
        - servicelb
      scheduler: false
      cloudController: false
      kubeProxy: false
      networkPolicy: false
      helmController: false

    tls:                               # API server TLS SANs
      sans:
        - lb.example.com
        - 10.0.0.100
      sanSecurity: true

    kubeconfig:                        # kubeconfig output settings
      mode: "0644"
      group: admin
      name: my-cluster

    datastore:                         # external datastore (MySQL/Postgres/etcd)
      endpoint: "postgres://user:pass@db:5432/k3s"
      caFile: /etc/ssl/ca.pem
      certFile: /etc/ssl/cert.pem
      keyFile: /etc/ssl/key.pem

    server:                            # API server listener settings
      advertiseAddress: 10.0.0.50
      advertisePort: 6443
      bindAddress: 0.0.0.0
      httpsPort: 6443

    security:                          # security hardening
      selinux: true
      protectKernelDefaults: true
      encryptionProvider: secretbox     # aescbc or secretbox

    componentArgs:                     # typed pass-through args for K3s components
      kubeAPIServer:
        - "--audit-log-path=/var/log/audit.log"
      kubeControllerManager:
        - "--node-cidr-mask-size=24"
      kubeScheduler: []
      kubeCloudControllerManager: []
      kubelet:
        - "--max-pods=110"
      kubeProxy:
        - "--proxy-mode=ipvs"
      etcd:
        - "--quota-backend-bytes=8589934592"
      helmController: []

    runtime:                           # container runtime settings
      systemDefaultRegistry: registry.example.com
      pauseImage: registry.example.com/pause:3.9
      snapshotter: stargz
      defaultRuntime: nvidia
      resolvConf: /etc/k3s-resolv.conf  # custom resolv.conf for containers

    embeddedRegistry:                  # built-in Spegel distributed registry
      enabled: true

    imageCredentialProvider:           # kubelet image credential provider
      binDir: /var/lib/rancher/credentialprovider/bin
      config: /var/lib/rancher/credentialprovider/config.yaml

    localStorage:                      # local-path provisioner settings
      path: /opt/local-path-provisioner

    etcdAdvanced:                      # advanced etcd tuning
      exposeMetrics: true
      disableSnapshots: false
      snapshotName: my-cluster
      snapshotReconcileInterval: 5m

  options:
    drain:
      enabled: true
      timeout: 5m
      gracePeriod: -1
      ignoreDaemonSets: true
      deleteEmptyDirData: true
      disableEviction: false
    concurrency:
      limit: 30
      uploads: 5
    evictTaint:
      enabled: false
```

## Hosts

`spec.hosts` is a list. Each entry describes one machine and the role it plays.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `role` | `server` (default) or `agent` |
| `ssh` / `openSSH` / `localhost` | How to reach the host |
| `privateAddress` | Address used for the node IP and API advertisements |
| `privateInterface` | Network interface whose address is used for node IP and API advertisements |
| `hostname` | Override the host name reported to the cluster |
| `installFlags` | Extra `k3s server` / `k3s agent` command-line flags |
| `labels`, `taints` | Convenience shortcuts for `--node-label` and `--node-taint` |
| `environment` | Environment variables written to the host and the systemd unit |
| `files` | Files to upload, from a local path or a URL |
| `hooks` | Commands to run before or after `apply` |
| `dataDir` | Overrides the K3s data directory |
| `uploadBinary` | Upload a locally built binary instead of downloading one |
| `k3sBinaryPath` | Use an existing binary already on the host |
| `nodeExternalIP` | List of external IPs advertised for the node (passed as `--node-external-ip`) |
| `nodeInternalDNS` | List of internal DNS names for the node |
| `nodeExternalDNS` | List of external DNS names for the node |
| `noFlannel` | Disable the flannel CNI |
| `os` | Override OS detection |

### SSH access

The `ssh` block takes an `address`, `user`, `port`, and `keyPath`. Use
`openSSH` to reuse your OpenSSH client configuration, or `localhost` when the
host is the machine running `k3sctl`.

### Files and hooks

`files` entries copy a local path or download a URL to `dst` on the host. Use
`perm` to set the mode. `hooks.apply.before` and `hooks.apply.after` run shell
commands around the apply step, which is useful for pre-flight checks and
post-install verification.

## K3s

`spec.k3s` controls the K3s installation itself.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `version` | K3s version to install, for example `v1.30.0+k3s1` |
| `config` | Mapping merged into `config.yaml` on every host |
| `extraArgs` | Extra arguments passed to the K3s service |
| `etcdSnapshots` | Automated etcd snapshot scheduling, S3 upload, and pruning |
| `secretsEncrypt` | Secrets encryption at rest with key rotation and re-encryption |
| `certRotate` | Rotate TLS certificates and optionally the root CA |
| `token` | Explicit server/agent join tokens and optional rotation |
| `registries` | Private registry mirrors and authentication |
| `healthCheck` | Post-apply cluster health verification |
| `preflight` | Pre-flight checks run before apply |
| `airgap` | Air-gap (offline) installation settings |
| `network` | Cluster and service CIDRs, DNS, flannel backend, egress mode, NodePort range |
| `disable` | Disable packaged components and individual K3s subsystems |
| `tls` | Subject Alternative Names for the API server certificate |
| `kubeconfig` | Write-kubeconfig mode, group, and name |
| `datastore` | External datastore endpoint (MySQL/Postgres/etcd) with TLS |
| `server` | API server advertise address/port, bind address, HTTPS port |
| `security` | SELinux, protect-kernel-defaults, encryption provider |
| `componentArgs` | Typed pass-through args for kube-apiserver, kubelet, etcd, and others |
| `runtime` | System default registry, pause image, snapshotter, default runtime, resolv.conf |
| `embeddedRegistry` | Enable the built-in Spegel distributed container registry |
| `imageCredentialProvider` | Kubelet image credential provider binary directory and config |
| `localStorage` | Custom path for the local-path provisioner |
| `etcdAdvanced` | Advanced etcd settings: metrics, snapshots, reconcile interval |

Binary sources can also be a URL, a local file, or an existing installation on
the host; see the host-level `uploadBinary` and `k3sBinaryPath` options above.

### etcdSnapshots

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `scheduled` | Enable scheduled snapshots |
| `scheduleCron` | Cron expression for the snapshot schedule |
| `retention` | Number of snapshots to retain |
| `dir` | Local directory for snapshots |
| `compress` | Compress snapshots |
| `s3.enabled` | Store snapshots in S3 |
| `s3.endpoint` | S3 endpoint |
| `s3.endpointCa` | Path to a CA certificate for the S3 endpoint |
| `s3.skipSslVerify` | Skip TLS verification for S3 |
| `s3.accessKey` | S3 access key |
| `s3.secretKey` | S3 secret key |
| `s3.bucket` | S3 bucket name (required when S3 is enabled) |
| `s3.region` | S3 region |
| `s3.folder` | Folder within the bucket |
| `s3.insecure` | Use HTTP instead of HTTPS |
| `s3.sessionToken` | STS session token for temporary AWS credentials |
| `s3.bucketLookupType` | Bucket lookup style: `auto`, `dns`, or `path` (default `auto`) |
| `s3.proxy` | HTTP proxy URL for S3 requests |
| `s3.configSecret` | Name of a Kubernetes secret containing the S3 configuration |
| `s3.timeout` | Timeout for S3 operations, for example `"30s"` |
| `s3.retention` | Per-S3 snapshot retention count (overrides the top-level `retention`) |

#### etcdSnapshots.prune

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable pruning of old etcd snapshots on apply |
| `retention` | Number of snapshots to retain (required when enabled, must be greater than 0) |
| `name` | Snapshot name filter for pruning, for example `on-demand` |

### secretsEncrypt

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable K3s secrets encryption at rest |
| `rotateKeys` | Dynamically rotate encryption keys |
| `reencrypt` | Re-encrypt all secrets with the new keys |

### certRotate

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Rotate K3s TLS certificates on each server during `apply` |
| `rotateCA` | Rotate the root Certificate Authority; triggers a full cluster restart |

### token

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `serverToken` | Token used for server-to-server communication |
| `agentToken` | Token used for agent-to-server communication |
| `rotate` | Rotate the cluster join token and restart all nodes |

### registries

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `mirrors.<registry>.endpoint` | List of mirror endpoint URLs for the given registry |
| `configs.<registry>.auth.username` | Registry authentication username |
| `configs.<registry>.auth.password` | Registry authentication password |
| `configs.<registry>.auth.token` | Registry authentication token |
| `configs.<registry>.tls.certFile` | Path to a client TLS certificate |
| `configs.<registry>.tls.keyFile` | Path to a client TLS key |
| `configs.<registry>.tls.caFile` | Path to a CA certificate for the registry |
| `configs.<registry>.tls.insecureSkipVerify` | Skip TLS verification for the registry |

The registries configuration is written to `/etc/rancher/k3s/registries.yaml`
on all nodes during apply.

### healthCheck

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable post-apply cluster health verification |
| `timeout` | Maximum wait time for health checks, for example `120s` or `5m` |

When enabled, the health check verifies the API server responds to `/healthz`
and all nodes reach `Ready` status before the apply completes.

### preflight

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable pre-flight checks |
| `checkCgroups` | Verify cgroup v1/v2 controllers are available |
| `checkModules` | Verify required kernel modules are loaded |
| `checkPorts` | Verify required ports are not in use |
| `checkDisk` | Verify minimum disk space is available |
| `minDiskGB` | Minimum disk space in GB |

### airgap

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable air-gap mode (skip downloading K3s images from the internet) |
| `imageBundle` | Local path to a K3s air-gap image bundle, for example `k3s-airgap-images-amd64.tar.zst` |

When enabled, the bundle is uploaded to `<dataDir>/agent/images/` on every host.

### network

Declarative cluster networking configuration. All fields are server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `clusterCIDR` | Pod CIDR ranges, for example `["10.42.0.0/16"]` or dual-stack `["10.42.0.0/16", "fd42::/48"]` |
| `serviceCIDR` | Service CIDR ranges, for example `["10.43.0.0/16"]` |
| `clusterDNS` | Cluster DNS service addresses, for example `["10.43.0.10"]` |
| `clusterDomain` | Cluster domain, for example `cluster.local` |
| `nodePortRange` | NodePort service port range, for example `"30000-32767"` |
| `flannelBackend` | Flannel backend: `none`, `vxlan`, `host-gw`, or `wireguard-native` |
| `flannelIPv6Masq` | Enable IPv6 masquerading for flannel |
| `flannelExternalIP` | Use node external IPs for flannel traffic |
| `flannelIface` | Network interface to use for flannel, for example `"eth1"` |
| `flannelConf` | Path to a custom flannel configuration file |
| `flannelCNIConf` | Path to a custom flannel CNI configuration file |
| `egressSelectorMode` | Egress selector mode: `agent`, `cluster`, `pod`, or `disabled` |
| `serviceLBNamespace` | Namespace for the built-in ServiceLB controller |

### disable

Disable packaged K3s components and subsystems. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `components` | List of packaged components to disable, for example `["traefik", "servicelb", "metrics-server", "coredns"]` |
| `scheduler` | Disable the kube-scheduler |
| `cloudController` | Disable the cloud controller manager |
| `kubeProxy` | Disable kube-proxy |
| `networkPolicy` | Disable the network policy controller |
| `helmController` | Disable the Helm controller |

### tls

TLS Subject Alternative Names for the API server certificate. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `sans` | Additional SANs for the API server TLS certificate, for example `["lb.example.com", "10.0.0.100"]` |
| `sanSecurity` | Enable TLS SAN security mode |

### kubeconfig

Controls how the admin kubeconfig file is written on server nodes. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `mode` | File permission mode for `kubeconfig`, for example `"0644"` |
| `group` | Group ownership for the kubeconfig file |
| `name` | Cluster name written into the kubeconfig |

### datastore

External datastore configuration for MySQL, PostgreSQL, or etcd. Server-only.
TLS fields require `endpoint` to be set.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `endpoint` | Datastore connection string, for example `"postgres://user:pass@db:5432/k3s"` |
| `caFile` | Path to the CA certificate for the datastore TLS connection |
| `certFile` | Path to the client certificate for the datastore TLS connection |
| `keyFile` | Path to the client key for the datastore TLS connection |

### server

API server listener settings. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `advertiseAddress` | Address the API server advertises to cluster members |
| `advertisePort` | Port the API server advertises (default `6443`) |
| `bindAddress` | Address the API server binds to, for example `"0.0.0.0"` |
| `httpsPort` | HTTPS listen port for the API server |

### security

Security hardening options. Applied to both server and agent nodes.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `selinux` | Enable SELinux support in K3s |
| `protectKernelDefaults` | Protect kernel defaults; K3s will error if required kernel parameters are not set |
| `encryptionProvider` | Secrets encryption provider: `aescbc` or `secretbox` |

### componentArgs

Typed pass-through arguments for Kubernetes components. Server-only args are
applied only to server configs; `kubelet` and `kubeProxy` are applied to both
server and agent configs.

| Key | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kubeAPIServer` | Server | Extra arguments for kube-apiserver |
| `kubeControllerManager` | Server | Extra arguments for kube-controller-manager |
| `kubeScheduler` | Server | Extra arguments for kube-scheduler |
| `kubeCloudControllerManager` | Server | Extra arguments for kube-cloud-controller-manager |
| `kubelet` | Server + Agent | Extra arguments for kubelet |
| `kubeProxy` | Server + Agent | Extra arguments for kube-proxy |
| `etcd` | Server | Extra arguments for etcd |
| `helmController` | Server | Extra arguments for the Helm controller |

### runtime

Container runtime settings. Applied to both server and agent nodes.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `systemDefaultRegistry` | Default registry for all system images, for example `"registry.example.com"` |
| `pauseImage` | Override the pause container image |
| `snapshotter` | Containerd snapshotter, for example `"stargz"` |
| `defaultRuntime` | Default container runtime, for example `"nvidia"` |
| `resolvConf` | Path to a custom `resolv.conf` for containers, for example `"/etc/k3s-resolv.conf"` |

### embeddedRegistry

Enable the built-in Spegel distributed container registry. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Enable the embedded Spegel distributed registry for peer-to-peer image sharing |

When enabled, K3s runs a built-in registry that distributes container images
across cluster nodes using peer-to-peer replication instead of pulling from an
external registry for every node.

### imageCredentialProvider

Kubelet image credential provider for authenticating with private container
registries. Applied to both server and agent nodes.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `binDir` | Directory containing credential provider plugin binaries (required) |
| `config` | Path to the credential provider configuration file (required) |

Both `binDir` and `config` must be set together. K3s passes them as
`--image-credential-provider-bin-dir` and `--image-credential-provider-config`.

### localStorage

Local-path provisioner settings. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `path` | Storage path used by the built-in local-path provisioner, for example `"/opt/local-path-provisioner"` |

### etcdAdvanced

Advanced etcd tuning options. Server-only.

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `exposeMetrics` | Expose etcd metrics to the `/metrics` endpoint |
| `disableSnapshots` | Disable automatic etcd snapshots |
| `snapshotName` | Name prefix for etcd snapshots |
| `snapshotReconcileInterval` | Interval for snapshot reconciliation, for example `"5m"` |

## Options

`spec.options` controls how `k3sctl` performs disruptive operations.

### Drain

`drain` controls how nodes are drained during upgrades and reconfiguration.

```yaml
spec:
  options:
    drain:
      enabled: true
      timeout: 5m
      gracePeriod: -1
      ignoreDaemonSets: true
      deleteEmptyDirData: true
      disableEviction: false
```

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Drain nodes before restarting them (default `true`) |
| `timeout` | Drain timeout (default `5m`) |
| `gracePeriod` | Grace period passed to `kubectl drain` (default `-1`) |
| `ignoreDaemonSets` | Ignore DaemonSet pods when draining (default `true`) |
| `deleteEmptyDirData` | Delete `emptyDir` data when draining (default `true`) |
| `disableEviction` | Force delete pods instead of evicting them (default `false`) |

### Concurrency

```yaml
spec:
  options:
    concurrency:
      limit: 30
      uploads: 5
```

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `limit` | Maximum number of hosts to process in parallel (default `30`) |
| `uploads` | Maximum number of concurrent file uploads (default `5`) |

### Evict taint

```yaml
spec:
  options:
    evictTaint:
      enabled: false
```

| Key | Description |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Taint nodes before eviction during disruptive operations (default `false`) |

## Additional manifests

Any other YAML documents in the configuration file are applied to the cluster
after installation. Separate them with `---`:

```yaml
# ... Cluster document ...
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: example
data:
  key: value
```

Each document must be a valid Kubernetes manifest. `k3sctl` passes them to
`kubectl apply` on the server node.

---

---
url: /docs/k3sctl/commands.md
description: The k3sctl CLI — apply, reset, kubeconfig, restore, config, init, and more.
---

# Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `k3sctl apply` | Install or update the cluster |
| `k3sctl reset` | Remove K3s from the hosts |
| `k3sctl kubeconfig` | Print the admin kubeconfig |
| `k3sctl restore` | Restore the cluster from an etcd snapshot |
| `k3sctl config diff` | Show differences between desired config and actual cluster state |
| `k3sctl config validate` | Validate a cluster configuration file |
| `k3sctl init` | Print a configuration template |
| `k3sctl version` | Print version information |
| `k3sctl completion` | Print a shell completion script |

## Global flags

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--debug` | Enable debug logging |
| `--trace` | Enable trace logging |
| `--no-redact` | Do not redact sensitive values from output |

## apply

`apply` reconciles the cluster with the configuration file. It is idempotent:
re-running it only changes what drifted.

```sh
k3sctl apply --config k3sctl.yaml
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change without changing it |
| `--no-wait` | Do not wait for the cluster to become ready |
| `--no-drain` | Skip node draining during the operation |
| `--restore-from` | Restore an etcd snapshot before applying |
| `--kubeconfig-out` | Write the admin kubeconfig to a file |
| `--kubeconfig-api-address` | Override the API address in the kubeconfig |
| `--kubeconfig-user` | Override the user in the kubeconfig |
| `--kubeconfig-cluster` | Override the cluster name in the kubeconfig |
| `--concurrency` | Number of hosts to operate on concurrently |
| `--concurrent-uploads` | Number of concurrent file uploads |
| `--disable-downgrade-check` | Allow installing an older K3s version |
| `--force` | Skip confirmation prompts |

## restore

`restore` stops K3s, resets etcd state, and restores the cluster from a
snapshot. It prompts for confirmation unless `--force` is given.

```sh
k3sctl restore --config k3sctl.yaml --from /path/to/snapshot.db
```

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--from` / `-f` | Path to the etcd snapshot to restore from (required) |
| `--force` | Skip the confirmation prompt |

## config

`config` groups configuration-only commands that do not change the cluster.

### diff

Preview what `apply` would change by comparing the desired configuration with
the actual cluster state.

```sh
k3sctl config diff --config k3sctl.yaml
```

### validate

Validate a configuration file without connecting to any host.

```sh
k3sctl config validate --config k3sctl.yaml
```

## Common workflows

### Create a cluster

```sh
k3sctl apply --config k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl kubeconfig > kubeconfig.yaml
export KUBECONFIG="$PWD/kubeconfig.yaml"
kubectl get nodes
```

### Validate and preview before applying

```sh
k3sctl config validate --config k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl config diff --config k3sctl.yaml
k3sctl apply --config k3sctl.yaml --dry-run
```

### Restore etcd

```sh
# Restore from a snapshot on the server
k3sctl restore --config k3sctl.yaml --from /path/to/snapshot.db
```

Snapshots are scheduled with the `etcdSnapshots` configuration block; see
[Configuration](./configuration.md) for scheduling, S3 upload, and pruning.

### Generate a starter file

```sh
k3sctl init --name demo --address 10.0.0.1 --agent --agent-address 10.0.0.2 > k3sctl.yaml
```

### Tear the cluster down

```sh
k3sctl reset --config k3sctl.yaml
```

## version and completion

```sh
k3sctl version
k3sctl completion bash
k3sctl completion zsh
```

---
url: /docs/mssql-mcp-go.md
description: >-
  A read-only Model Context Protocol server for Microsoft SQL Server, written in
  Go, with 70+ tools for schema, data, performance, security, and migration
  analysis.
---

# mssql-mcp-go

`mssql-mcp-go` is a **read-only** [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
(MCP) server for Microsoft SQL Server, written in Go. It gives AI assistants
safe, structured access to your databases for schema exploration, data
profiling, query analysis, migration planning, and more.

## Why read-only

Every query is validated before execution. `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`,
`DROP`, `ALTER`, `CREATE`, `TRUNCATE`, and other mutating statements are
rejected before they reach the database. Stored procedures and functions are
analyzed statically and never executed.

That makes the server safe to hand to an assistant that needs to understand a
production database without being able to change it.

## Features

* **Read-only by design** — mutating SQL is blocked by a validator.
* **70+ tools** covering schema discovery, data profiling, performance
  analysis, security auditing, migration assessment, and monitoring.
* **Always Encrypted support** — client-side column decryption with a local PFX
  certificate.
* **Connection pooling** with configurable limits and automatic cleanup.
* **Stdio transport** for Claude Desktop, Cline, and other MCP clients.
* **Single binary** for Linux, macOS, and Windows, plus a multi-arch container
  image.

## Quick start

Set the connection with environment variables (they always override the config
file), then run the server:

```sh
export SQLSERVER_HOST=localhost
export SQLSERVER_PORT=1433
export SQLSERVER_USER=readonly_user
export SQLSERVER_PASSWORD=secret
export SQLSERVER_DATABASE=MyDatabase

mssql-mcp-go
```

The server starts on stdio by default and waits for an MCP client to connect.
See [Configuration](./configuration.md) for `config.yaml` and client setup, and
[Tools](./tools.md) for the full tool list.

## Architecture

```
mssql-mcp-go/
  cmd/server/            Entry point
  internal/
    adapters/mcp/        MCP protocol, tool registration
    mssql/               Service layer (queries, analysis)
    db/                  Connection pool, query execution, encryption
    infrastructure/      Config, logging
  pkg/version/           Build version info
```

The server registers all tools with the MCP SDK and forwards tool calls to the
SQL Server service layer. Every statement passes through the read-only
validator first.

## Next steps

* [Installation](./installation.md)
* [Configuration](./configuration.md)
* [Tools](./tools.md)

---

---
url: /docs/mssql-mcp-go/installation.md
description: Install mssql-mcp-go with Homebrew, a release binary, Docker, or from source.
---

# Installation

## Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install vinaycharlie01/tap/mssql-mcp-go
```

## Download a binary

Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows (`amd64` / `arm64`) are
published with every [GitHub release](https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go/releases).

```sh
# Example: the latest release for macOS arm64
curl -LO https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go/releases/latest/download/mssql-mcp-go_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
tar xzf mssql-mcp-go_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
sudo mv mssql-mcp-go /usr/local/bin/
```

## Docker

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go:latest

docker run --rm \
  -e SQLSERVER_HOST=host.docker.internal \
  -e SQLSERVER_PORT=1433 \
  -e SQLSERVER_USER=readonly_user \
  -e SQLSERVER_PASSWORD=secret \
  -e SQLSERVER_DATABASE=MyDatabase \
  ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go:latest
```

## Build from source

Requires Go 1.25 or newer.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go.git
cd mssql-mcp-go
go build -o dist/mssql-mcp-go ./cmd/server
```

The binary is written to `dist/mssql-mcp-go`.

## Configure and run

The server reads `config.yaml` or environment variables. To start from the
example file:

```sh
cp config.yaml.example config.yaml
# edit config.yaml with your database credentials
mssql-mcp-go
```

The default transport is stdio, so the process waits for an MCP client on
standard input. See [Configuration](./configuration.md) for every option and
the Claude Desktop and Cline snippets.

---

---
url: /docs/mssql-mcp-go/configuration.md
description: >-
  Configure mssql-mcp-go with config.yaml or environment variables, and connect
  it to Claude Desktop, Cline, or Docker.
---

# Configuration

The server reads settings from a `config.yaml` file or from environment
variables. **Environment variables always override the file**, which makes
secrets easy to inject at runtime.

## config.yaml

Start from `config.yaml.example`:

```yaml
database:
  host: "localhost"
  port: 1433
  user: "readonly_user"
  password: ""              # prefer SQLSERVER_PASSWORD
  database: "MyDatabase"
  encrypt: "true"           # true, false, or disable
  trust_server_certificate: false
  connection_timeout: 30

# Always Encrypted: client-side column decryption with a local PFX.
encryption:
  enabled: false
  key_path: ""              # absolute path to the .pfx file
  key_password: ""          # prefer SQLSERVER_ALWAYS_ENCRYPTED_KEY_PASSWORD

query:
  max_length: 5000          # max characters per query
  max_rows: 1000            # max rows returned
  timeout: 30s              # per-query timeout

pool:
  max_open_conns: 10
  max_idle_conns: 5
  conn_max_lifetime: 1h

logging:
  level: "info"             # debug, info, warn, error
  format: "json"            # json, text

mcp:
  transport: "stdio"        # stdio or http
  port: 9090
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `SQLSERVER_HOST` | Database host |
| `SQLSERVER_PORT` | Database port (default `1433`) |
| `SQLSERVER_USER` | Database user |
| `SQLSERVER_PASSWORD` | Database password |
| `SQLSERVER_DATABASE` | Database name |
| `SQLSERVER_ENCRYPT` | Encryption mode (default `true`) |
| `SQLSERVER_TRUST_SERVER_CERTIFICATE` | Trust self-signed certificates |
| `SQLSERVER_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT` | Connection timeout in seconds |
| `SQLSERVER_ALWAYS_ENCRYPTED_KEY_PATH` | Path to the PFX certificate |
| `SQLSERVER_ALWAYS_ENCRYPTED_KEY_PASSWORD` | PFX certificate password |
| `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH` | Maximum query length |
| `QUERY_MAX_ROWS` | Maximum result rows |
| `QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-query timeout |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | Log level |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | Log format |
| `CONFIG_PATH` | Path to `config.yaml` |

## MCP client integration

### Claude Desktop

Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mssql": {
      "command": "mssql-mcp-go",
      "env": {
        "SQLSERVER_HOST": "localhost",
        "SQLSERVER_PORT": "1433",
        "SQLSERVER_USER": "readonly_user",
        "SQLSERVER_PASSWORD": "secret",
        "SQLSERVER_DATABASE": "MyDatabase",
        "SQLSERVER_ENCRYPT": "disable"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If you installed with Homebrew, the binary is already on your `PATH`.
Otherwise, use its full path.

### Claude Desktop with Docker

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mssql": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "run", "--rm", "-i",
        "-e", "SQLSERVER_HOST=host.docker.internal",
        "-e", "SQLSERVER_PORT=1433",
        "-e", "SQLSERVER_USER=readonly_user",
        "-e", "SQLSERVER_PASSWORD=secret",
        "-e", "SQLSERVER_DATABASE=MyDatabase",
        "ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/mssql-mcp-go:latest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Cline (VS Code)

Add the server to your Cline MCP settings:

```json
{
  "mssql": {
    "command": "mssql-mcp-go",
    "env": {
      "SQLSERVER_HOST": "localhost",
      "SQLSERVER_PORT": "1433",
      "SQLSERVER_USER": "readonly_user",
      "SQLSERVER_PASSWORD": "secret",
      "SQLSERVER_DATABASE": "MyDatabase"
    }
  }
}
```

## Security notes

* Use a login that only has read permissions on the databases the assistant
  should see.
* Prefer environment variables over committing credentials to `config.yaml`.
* TLS is on by default (`encrypt: true`). Set `trust_server_certificate: false`
  unless you are connecting to a server with a self-signed certificate.
* Always Encrypted columns are decrypted client-side with the PFX you provide;
  the key never leaves the machine running the server.

url: /docs/mssql-mcp-go/tools.md
description: All tools exposed by mssql-mcp-go, grouped by what they help you do.

# Tools

Every tool below issues read-only catalog queries or validated `SELECT` /
`WITH` statements. Mutating SQL is rejected before execution.

## Core query

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `execute_query` | Run a read-only `SELECT` / `WITH` query |
| `health_check` | Check connectivity and connection-pool stats |

## Database discovery

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_databases` | List accessible databases |
| `list_schemas` | List schemas in the current database |
| `list_tables` | List tables with row and column counts |
| `describe_table` | Columns, keys, and indexes of a table |
| `list_columns` | Columns with types and nullability |
| `describe_column` | Detailed metadata for a single column |
| `table_row_count` | Row count from catalog metadata |

## Relationships and keys

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `table_relationships` | Outbound and inbound foreign keys |
| `list_foreign_keys` | Foreign-key constraints, optionally by schema |
| `list_primary_keys` | Primary-key constraints, optionally by schema |
| `foreign_key_graph` | Full foreign-key graph as nodes and edges |
| `list_unique_constraints` | Unique constraints by schema |
| `list_check_constraints` | Check constraints by schema |
| `list_default_constraints` | Default constraints by schema |

## Stored procedures

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_procedures` | List stored procedures |
| `get_procedure_definition` | Full T-SQL definition and parameters |
| `search_procedures` | Search definitions by keyword |
| `analyze_stored_procedure` | Static analysis: tables, views, transactions, and more |
| `extract_tables_used` | Tables referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_views_used` | Views referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_functions_used` | Functions referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_called_procedures` | Procedures called with `EXEC` |
| `extract_transaction_usage` | Transaction-control usage |
| `extract_dynamic_sql` | Dynamic SQL detection |
| `extract_cursor_usage` | Cursor declarations |
| `extract_temp_tables` | Temp-table usage |
| `extract_error_handling` | Error-handling constructs |
| `extract_validation_rules` | Validation rules |
| `extract_business_rules` | Business-rule comments |

## Views

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_views` | List all views |
| `get_view_definition` | Definition of a view |
| `analyze_view` | Columns and referenced objects |
| `trace_view_sources` | Resolve underlying base tables |
| `extract_view_dependencies` | Objects a view depends on |

## Functions

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_functions` | Scalar, inline, and table-valued functions |
| `get_function_definition` | Definition and parameters |
| `analyze_function` | Static analysis |
| `trace_function_usage` | Objects referencing the function |
| `extract_function_dependencies` | Objects a function depends on |

## Triggers

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_triggers` | DML triggers with their tables |
| `get_trigger_definition` | Definition of a trigger |
| `analyze_trigger` | Static analysis |

## Dependencies and search

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `find_object_dependencies` | Objects an object depends on |
| `find_object_references` | Objects that reference an object |
| `find_table_usage` | All objects referencing a table |
| `search_objects_by_keyword` | Search names and definitions |
| `generate_erd` | Entity-relationship description |
| `dependency_graph` | Recursive dependency graph |
| `find_column_usage` | Modules referencing a column |
| `find_unused_tables` | Tables with no references |
| `find_unused_columns` | Columns with no tracked references |
| `find_orphan_tables` | Tables with no foreign-key connections |
| `find_circular_dependencies` | Cycles in the foreign-key graph |
| `search_tables` | Tables matching a keyword |
| `search_columns` | Columns matching a keyword |
| `search_views` | Views matching a keyword |
| `search_functions` | Functions matching a keyword |

## Data profiling

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `table_statistics` | Row count, column count, and storage stats |
| `column_statistics` | Min, max, distinct, and null statistics |
| `column_distinct_values` | Top distinct values with frequencies |
| `column_null_analysis` | Null count and percentage |
| `data_distribution` | Value-frequency distribution |
| `sample_table_data` | Sample rows from a table |
| `find_duplicate_rows` | Duplicate groups by columns |
| `find_candidate_keys` | Single-column candidate-key detection |

## Performance analysis

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `explain_query` | Estimated execution plan |
| `estimate_query_cost` | Estimated subtree cost |
| `analyze_execution_plan` | Plan with an operator summary |
| `find_missing_indexes` | Optimizer-recommended indexes |
| `find_unused_indexes` | Indexes that are never read |
| `find_fragmented_indexes` | High-fragmentation indexes |
| `index_usage_report` | Read and write stats for all indexes |
| `slow_query_analysis` | Most expensive cached queries |
| `query_performance_report` | Aggregate query stats |

## Security analysis

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_logins` | Server-level logins |
| `list_users` | Database-level users |
| `list_roles` | Database roles |
| `list_permissions` | Database permission grants |
| `user_permissions` | Permissions for a specific user |
| `role_memberships` | Role-membership graph |
| `object_permissions` | Permissions on a specific object |

## Migration assessment

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `database_overview` | High-level object counts |
| `database_health_report` | Health indicators |
| `database_complexity_report` | Structural complexity metrics |
| `analyze_database_for_migration` | Comprehensive migration assessment |
| `migration_complexity_score` | Weighted complexity score |
| `migration_priority_order` | Dependency-based migration order |
| `high_risk_objects` | Modules with risky constructs |
| `large_table_analysis` | Largest tables by storage |
| `legacy_object_analysis` | Stale or legacy objects |
| `deprecated_feature_detection` | Deprecated-feature scan |

## Monitoring

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `connection_pool_stats` | Connection-pool statistics |
| `database_size_report` | Data and log file sizes |
| `table_growth_report` | Largest tables by size |

# postgres-mcp-go

`postgres-mcp-go` is a **read-only** [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
(MCP) server for PostgreSQL, written in Go. It gives AI assistants safe,
structured access to your databases for schema exploration, data profiling,
query analysis, migration planning, and more.

## Why read-only

Every query is validated before execution. `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`,
`DROP`, `ALTER`, `CREATE`, `TRUNCATE`, and other mutating statements are
rejected before they reach the database. Stored procedures and functions are
analyzed statically and never executed.

That makes the server safe to hand to an assistant that needs to understand a
production database without being able to change it.

## Features

* **Read-only by design** — mutating SQL is blocked by a validator.
* **70+ tools** covering schema discovery, data profiling, performance
  analysis, security auditing, migration assessment, and monitoring.
* **Connection pooling** with configurable limits and automatic cleanup.
* **Stdio transport** for Claude Desktop, Cline, and other MCP clients.
* **Single binary** for Linux, macOS, and Windows, plus a multi-arch container
  image.

## Quick start

Set the connection with environment variables (they always override the config
file), then run the server:

```sh
export POSTGRES_HOST=localhost
export POSTGRES_PORT=5432
export POSTGRES_USER=readonly_user
export POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret
export POSTGRES_DB=mydb

postgres-mcp-go
```

The server starts on stdio by default and waits for an MCP client to connect.
See [Configuration](./configuration.md) for `config.yaml` and client setup, and
[Tools](./tools.md) for the full tool list.

## Architecture

```
postgres-mcp-go/
  cmd/server/            Entry point
  internal/
    adapters/mcp/        MCP protocol, tool registration
    postgres/            Service layer (queries, analysis)
    db/                  Connection pool, query execution
    infrastructure/      Config, logging
  pkg/version/           Build version info
```

The server registers all tools with the MCP SDK and forwards tool calls to the
PostgreSQL service layer. Every statement passes through the read-only validator
first.

## Next steps

* [Installation](./installation.md)
* [Configuration](./configuration.md)
* [Tools](./tools.md)

---

---
url: /docs/postgres-mcp-go/installation.md
description: >-
  Install postgres-mcp-go with Homebrew, a release binary, Docker, or from
  source.
---

# Installation

## Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```sh
brew install vinaycharlie01/tap/postgres-mcp-go
```

## Download a binary

Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows (`amd64` / `arm64`) are
published with every [GitHub release](https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go/releases).

```sh
# Example: the latest release for macOS arm64
curl -LO https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go/releases/latest/download/postgres-mcp-go_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
tar xzf postgres-mcp-go_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
sudo mv postgres-mcp-go /usr/local/bin/
```

## Docker

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go:latest

docker run --rm \
  -e POSTGRES_HOST=host.docker.internal \
  -e POSTGRES_PORT=5432 \
  -e POSTGRES_USER=readonly_user \
  -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret \
  -e POSTGRES_DB=mydb \
  ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go:latest
```

## Build from source

Requires Go 1.27 or newer.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go.git
cd postgres-mcp-go
go build -o dist/postgres-mcp-go ./cmd/server
```

The binary is written to `dist/postgres-mcp-go`.

## Configure and run

The server reads `config.yaml` or environment variables. To start from the
example file:

```sh
cp config.yaml.example config.yaml
# edit config.yaml with your database credentials
postgres-mcp-go
```

The default transport is stdio, so the process waits for an MCP client on
standard input. See [Configuration](./configuration.md) for every option and
the Claude Desktop and Cline snippets.

---

---
url: /docs/postgres-mcp-go/configuration.md
description: >-
  Configure postgres-mcp-go with config.yaml or environment variables, and
  connect it to Claude Desktop, Cline, or Docker.
---

# Configuration

The server reads settings from a `config.yaml` file or from environment
variables. **Environment variables always override the file**, which makes
secrets easy to inject at runtime.

## config.yaml

Start from `config.yaml.example`:

```yaml
database:
  host: "localhost"
  port: 5432
  user: "readonly_user"
  password: ""              # prefer POSTGRES_PASSWORD
  database: "postgres"
  ssl_mode: "require"       # disable, allow, prefer, require, verify-ca, verify-full
  search_path: "public"
  connection_timeout: 30

query:
  max_length: 5000          # max characters per query
  max_rows: 1000            # max rows returned
  timeout: 30s              # per-query timeout

pool:
  max_open_conns: 10
  max_idle_conns: 5
  conn_max_lifetime: 1h

logging:
  level: "info"             # debug, info, warn, error
  format: "json"            # json, text
  file: ""                  # optional log file path

mcp:
  transport: "stdio"        # stdio or http
  port: 9090
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `POSTGRES_HOST` | Database host |
| `POSTGRES_PORT` | Database port (default `5432`) |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | Database user |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Database password |
| `POSTGRES_DB` | Database name |
| `POSTGRES_SSL_MODE` | TLS mode (default `require`) |
| `POSTGRES_SEARCH_PATH` | Default schema (default `public`) |
| `POSTGRES_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT` | Connection timeout in seconds |
| `QUERY_MAX_LENGTH` | Maximum query length |
| `QUERY_MAX_ROWS` | Maximum result rows |
| `QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-query timeout |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | Log level |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | Log format |
| `LOG_FILE` | Log file path |
| `CONFIG_PATH` | Path to `config.yaml` |

## MCP client integration

### Claude Desktop

Add the server to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "postgres": {
      "command": "postgres-mcp-go",
      "env": {
        "POSTGRES_HOST": "localhost",
        "POSTGRES_PORT": "5432",
        "POSTGRES_USER": "readonly_user",
        "POSTGRES_PASSWORD": "secret",
        "POSTGRES_DB": "mydb",
        "POSTGRES_SSL_MODE": "disable"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If you installed with Homebrew, the binary is already on your `PATH`.
Otherwise, use its full path.

### Claude Desktop with Docker

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "postgres": {
      "command": "docker",
      "args": [
        "run", "--rm", "-i",
        "-e", "POSTGRES_HOST=host.docker.internal",
        "-e", "POSTGRES_PORT=5432",
        "-e", "POSTGRES_USER=readonly_user",
        "-e", "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret",
        "-e", "POSTGRES_DB=mydb",
        "ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/postgres-mcp-go:latest"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Cline (VS Code)

Add the server to your Cline MCP settings:

```json
{
  "postgres": {
    "command": "postgres-mcp-go",
    "env": {
      "POSTGRES_HOST": "localhost",
      "POSTGRES_PORT": "5432",
      "POSTGRES_USER": "readonly_user",
      "POSTGRES_PASSWORD": "secret",
      "POSTGRES_DB": "mydb"
    }
  }
}
```

## Security notes

* Use a role that only has read permissions on the databases the assistant
  should see.
* Prefer environment variables over committing credentials to `config.yaml`.
* TLS is on by default (`ssl_mode: require`). Use `verify-full` in production,
  and reserve `disable` for trusted local networks.
* Set `search_path` when the objects live outside `public`, so unqualified names
  resolve as expected.

# Tools

Every tool below issues read-only catalog queries or validated `SELECT` /
`WITH` statements. Mutating SQL is rejected before execution.

## Core query

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `execute_query` | Run a read-only `SELECT` / `WITH` query |
| `health_check` | Check connectivity and connection-pool stats |

## Database discovery

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_databases` | List accessible databases |
| `list_schemas` | List schemas in the current database |
| `list_tables` | List tables with row and column counts |
| `describe_table` | Columns, keys, and indexes of a table |
| `list_columns` | Columns with types and nullability |
| `describe_column` | Detailed metadata for a single column |
| `table_row_count` | Row count from catalog metadata |

## Relationships and keys

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `table_relationships` | Outbound and inbound foreign keys |
| `list_foreign_keys` | Foreign-key constraints, optionally by schema |
| `list_primary_keys` | Primary-key constraints, optionally by schema |
| `foreign_key_graph` | Full foreign-key graph as nodes and edges |
| `list_unique_constraints` | Unique constraints by schema |
| `list_check_constraints` | Check constraints by schema |
| `list_default_constraints` | Default constraints by schema |

## Stored procedures

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_procedures` | List stored procedures |
| `get_procedure_definition` | Full T-SQL definition and parameters |
| `search_procedures` | Search definitions by keyword |
| `analyze_stored_procedure` | Static analysis: tables, views, transactions, and more |
| `extract_tables_used` | Tables referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_views_used` | Views referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_functions_used` | Functions referenced by a procedure |
| `extract_called_procedures` | Procedures called with `EXEC` |
| `extract_transaction_usage` | Transaction-control usage |
| `extract_dynamic_sql` | Dynamic SQL detection |
| `extract_cursor_usage` | Cursor declarations |
| `extract_temp_tables` | Temp-table usage |
| `extract_error_handling` | Error-handling constructs |
| `extract_validation_rules` | Validation rules |
| `extract_business_rules` | Business-rule comments |

## Views

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_views` | List all views |
| `get_view_definition` | Definition of a view |
| `analyze_view` | Columns and referenced objects |
| `trace_view_sources` | Resolve underlying base tables |
| `extract_view_dependencies` | Objects a view depends on |

## Functions

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_functions` | Scalar, inline, and table-valued functions |
| `get_function_definition` | Definition and parameters |
| `analyze_function` | Static analysis |
| `trace_function_usage` | Objects referencing the function |
| `extract_function_dependencies` | Objects a function depends on |

## Triggers

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_triggers` | DML triggers with their tables |
| `get_trigger_definition` | Definition of a trigger |
| `analyze_trigger` | Static analysis |

## Dependencies and search

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `find_object_dependencies` | Objects an object depends on |
| `find_object_references` | Objects that reference an object |
| `find_table_usage` | All objects referencing a table |
| `search_objects_by_keyword` | Search names and definitions |
| `generate_erd` | Entity-relationship description |
| `dependency_graph` | Recursive dependency graph |
| `find_column_usage` | Modules referencing a column |
| `find_unused_tables` | Tables with no references |
| `find_unused_columns` | Columns with no tracked references |
| `find_orphan_tables` | Tables with no foreign-key connections |
| `find_circular_dependencies` | Cycles in the foreign-key graph |
| `search_tables` | Tables matching a keyword |
| `search_columns` | Columns matching a keyword |
| `search_views` | Views matching a keyword |
| `search_functions` | Functions matching a keyword |

## Data profiling

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `table_statistics` | Row count, column count, and storage stats |
| `column_statistics` | Min, max, distinct, and null statistics |
| `column_distinct_values` | Top distinct values with frequencies |
| `column_null_analysis` | Null count and percentage |
| `data_distribution` | Value-frequency distribution |
| `sample_table_data` | Sample rows from a table |
| `find_duplicate_rows` | Duplicate groups by columns |
| `find_candidate_keys` | Single-column candidate-key detection |

## Performance analysis

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `explain_query` | Estimated execution plan |
| `estimate_query_cost` | Estimated subtree cost |
| `analyze_execution_plan` | Plan with an operator summary |
| `find_missing_indexes` | Optimizer-recommended indexes |
| `find_unused_indexes` | Indexes that are never read |
| `find_fragmented_indexes` | High-fragmentation indexes |
| `index_usage_report` | Read and write stats for all indexes |
| `slow_query_analysis` | Most expensive cached queries |
| `query_performance_report` | Aggregate query stats |

## Security analysis

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `list_logins` | Server-level logins |
| `list_users` | Database-level users |
| `list_roles` | Database roles |
| `list_permissions` | Database permission grants |
| `user_permissions` | Permissions for a specific user |
| `role_memberships` | Role-membership graph |
| `object_permissions` | Permissions on a specific object |

## Migration assessment

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `database_overview` | High-level object counts |
| `database_health_report` | Health indicators |
| `database_complexity_report` | Structural complexity metrics |
| `analyze_database_for_migration` | Comprehensive migration assessment |
| `migration_complexity_score` | Weighted complexity score |
| `migration_priority_order` | Dependency-based migration order |
| `high_risk_objects` | Modules with risky constructs |
| `large_table_analysis` | Largest tables by storage |
| `legacy_object_analysis` | Stale or legacy objects |
| `deprecated_feature_detection` | Deprecated-feature scan |

## Monitoring

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `connection_pool_stats` | Connection-pool statistics |
| `database_size_report` | Data and log file sizes |
| `table_growth_report` | Largest tables by size |

url: /docs/omniroute-operator.md
description: >-
  A Kubebuilder operator that deploys and manages OmniRoute — the unified AI
  proxy/router — on self-hosted Kubernetes.
---

# omniroute-operator

`omniroute-operator` is a Kubernetes operator built with
[Kubebuilder](https://kubebuilder.io/) that deploys and manages
[OmniRoute](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute), a unified AI
proxy/router, in self-hosted Kubernetes environments.

The operator watches `OmniRoute` custom resources and reconciles Deployments,
Services, PersistentVolumeClaims, and Ingresses, so you get a managed OmniRoute
instance from a single `kubectl apply`.

## Features

* Declarative lifecycle via the `gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1` CRD.
* Automatic Deployment, Service, PVC, and Ingress reconciliation.
* Credentials injected from existing Secrets.
* Configuration injected from an existing ConfigMap with `envFrom`.
* Auto-derived `NODE_OPTIONS` from memory limits to prevent OOM kills.
* Configurable liveness, readiness, and startup probes.
* Redis-backed rate limiting, from a URL or a Secret.
* Database encryption at rest with `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
* Ingress with TLS, `className`, and annotations.
* Reverse-proxy support through `basePath`.
* Service annotations for cloud load balancers.
* Persistence for OmniRoute's SQLite data directory.
* Leader election for highly available operator deployments.
* Multi-arch images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) and a Helm chart.

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| Kubernetes | >= 1.28 |
| Helm | >= 3.12 |
| kubectl | matching your cluster |

For local development you also need k3d >= 5.6, Docker >= 24, and Go 1.27.

## How it works

1. You install the operator and its CRD into `omniroute-system`.
2. You create a Secret with OmniRoute's credentials and, optionally, a
   ConfigMap with environment settings.
3. You apply an `OmniRoute` resource in your application namespace.
4. The operator creates the Deployment, Service, PVC, and (when enabled) the
   Ingress, then reports readiness on the resource status.

## Deploy a first instance

```sh
kubectl create secret generic omniroute-secrets \
  --namespace ai-platform \
  --from-literal=JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 48)" \
  --from-literal=API_KEY_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --from-literal=INITIAL_PASSWORD="changeme"

kubectl apply -f config/samples/gateway_v1alpha1_omniroute.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=available deployment/omniroute-sample \
  --namespace ai-platform --timeout=120s
```

Then reach the UI:

```sh
kubectl port-forward svc/omniroute-sample 20128:20128 -n ai-platform
```

Open `http://localhost:20128` and log in with the password from
`INITIAL_PASSWORD`.

## Next steps

* [Installation](./installation.md): install the operator with Helm.
* [OmniRoute CR](./omniroute-cr.md): every field in the custom resource.
* [Local development](./local-development.md): a k3d cluster on your machine.

---

---
url: /docs/omniroute-operator/installation.md
description: Install the omniroute-operator with Helm, then deploy an OmniRoute instance.
---

# Installation

The operator and the OmniRoute instances it manages are separate concerns. You
install the operator once per cluster; each application namespace then gets one
or more `OmniRoute` resources.

## Install the operator

From the OCI registry:

```sh
helm install omniroute-operator oci://ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/helm-charts/omniroute-operator \
  --namespace omniroute-system --create-namespace
```

Or from the chart in the repository:

```sh
helm install omniroute-operator charts/omniroute-operator \
  --namespace omniroute-system --create-namespace
```

Verify the controller is running:

```sh
kubectl get pods -n omniroute-system
```

## Helm values

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `replicaCount` | `1` | Operator pod replicas |
| `image.repository` | `ghcr.io/vinaycharlie01/omniroute-operator` | Operator image |
| `image.tag` | `""` (appVersion) | Operator image tag |
| `leaderElection.enabled` | `true` | Enable leader election |
| `resources.requests.cpu` | `10m` | CPU request |
| `resources.requests.memory` | `64Mi` | Memory request |
| `resources.limits.cpu` | `500m` | CPU limit |
| `resources.limits.memory` | `128Mi` | Memory limit |

## Create the OmniRoute secrets

OmniRoute requires three secrets: `JWT_SECRET`, `API_KEY_SECRET`, and
`INITIAL_PASSWORD`.

```sh
kubectl create secret generic omniroute-secrets \
  --namespace ai-platform \
  --from-literal=JWT_SECRET="$(openssl rand -base64 48)" \
  --from-literal=API_KEY_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" \
  --from-literal=INITIAL_PASSWORD="changeme"
```

## Optional: environment configuration

All keys in the referenced ConfigMap are injected into the OmniRoute container
as environment variables with `envFrom`:

```sh
kubectl create configmap omniroute-config \
  --namespace ai-platform \
  --from-literal=PORT=20128 \
  --from-literal=APP_LOG_LEVEL=info \
  --from-literal=REQUIRE_API_KEY=false
```

## Deploy an instance

```sh
kubectl apply -f config/samples/gateway_v1alpha1_omniroute.yaml
```

Or apply a minimal resource inline:

```sh
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1
kind: OmniRoute
metadata:
  name: omniroute
  namespace: ai-platform
spec:
  image:
    repository: diegosouzapw/omniroute
    tag: "3.8.51"
  replicas: 1
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 20128
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 250m
      memory: 512Mi
    limits:
      cpu: "1"
      memory: 1Gi
  credentials:
    existingSecret: omniroute-secrets
  config:
    existingConfigMap: omniroute-config
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 1Gi
EOF
```

Wait for the Deployment, then reach the UI:

```sh
kubectl wait --for=condition=available deployment/omniroute \
  --namespace ai-platform --timeout=120s

kubectl port-forward svc/omniroute 20128:20128 -n ai-platform
```

Open `http://localhost:20128` and log in with `INITIAL_PASSWORD`.

## Expose OmniRoute

The CR supports `ClusterIP`, `NodePort`, `LoadBalancer`, and Ingress. See
[OmniRoute CR](./omniroute-cr.md) for the Service and Ingress fields, and the
complete spec reference.

```yaml
spec:
  ingress:
    enabled: true
    className: nginx
    host: omniroute.example.com
    annotations:
      cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
    tls:
      secretName: omniroute-tls
```

## Use the API

OmniRoute exposes an OpenAI-compatible API:

```sh
curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-4o",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}]
  }'
```

## Uninstall

```sh
kubectl delete omniroute omniroute -n ai-platform
helm uninstall omniroute-operator -n omniroute-system
```

---

---
url: /docs/omniroute-operator/omniroute-cr.md
description: Reference for the gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1 OmniRoute custom resource.
---

# OmniRoute CR

An `OmniRoute` resource describes one OmniRoute deployment. The operator
reconciles a Deployment, Service, PVC, and optional Ingress from it.

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1
kind: OmniRoute
metadata:
  name: omniroute
  namespace: ai-platform
spec:
  image:
    repository: diegosouzapw/omniroute
    tag: "3.8.51"
  replicas: 1
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 20128
  credentials:
    existingSecret: omniroute-secrets
  config:
    existingConfigMap: omniroute-config
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    size: 1Gi
```

## Core

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.image.repository` | string | `diegosouzapw/omniroute` | OmniRoute container image |
| `spec.image.tag` | string | `3.8.51` | Image tag |
| `spec.image.pullPolicy` | string | `IfNotPresent` | Image pull policy |
| `spec.replicas` | int | `1` | Pod count (max 1 — SQLite is single-writer) |
| `spec.resources` | ResourceRequirements | — | CPU and memory requests and limits |
| `spec.env` | \[]EnvVar | — | Additional environment variables |

## Service

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.service.type` | string | `ClusterIP` | `ClusterIP`, `NodePort`, or `LoadBalancer` |
| `spec.service.port` | int | `20128` | Service port |
| `spec.service.annotations` | map\[string]string | — | Service annotations, for example for an AWS NLB |

## Configuration and credentials

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.config.existingConfigMap` | string | — | ConfigMap with OmniRoute environment variables (injected with `envFrom`) |
| `spec.credentials.existingSecret` | string | — | Secret with `JWT_SECRET`, `API_KEY_SECRET`, and `INITIAL_PASSWORD` |

## Persistence

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.persistence.enabled` | bool | `true` | Create a PVC for the data directory |
| `spec.persistence.size` | string | `1Gi` | PVC storage size |
| `spec.persistence.storageClass` | string | cluster default | StorageClass name |
| `spec.persistence.accessMode` | string | `ReadWriteOnce` | PVC access mode |

## Health probes

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.probes.livenessPath` | string | `/api/monitoring/health` | HTTP path for the liveness probe |
| `spec.probes.readinessPath` | string | `/api/monitoring/health` | HTTP path for the readiness probe |
| `spec.probes.startupPath` | string | `/api/monitoring/health` | HTTP path for the startup probe |

The operator fills in sensible timing defaults for all three probes.

## Ingress

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.ingress.enabled` | bool | `false` | Create an Ingress resource |
| `spec.ingress.className` | string | — | IngressClass name, such as `nginx` |
| `spec.ingress.host` | string | — | Hostname for the Ingress rule |
| `spec.ingress.tls.secretName` | string | — | TLS Secret name |
| `spec.ingress.annotations` | map\[string]string | — | Ingress annotations |

## Redis (rate limiting)

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.redis.url` | string | — | Redis connection URL, such as `redis://redis:6379` |
| `spec.redis.existingSecret` | string | — | Secret containing a `REDIS_URL` key |
| `spec.redis.keyPrefix` | string | — | Redis key namespace prefix |

## Encryption (database at rest)

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.encryption.existingSecret` | string | — | Secret containing `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` |
| `spec.encryption.keyVersion` | string | — | Encryption key version, for key rotation |

## Reverse proxy

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spec.basePath` | string | — | Sets `OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH`, for example `/omniroute` |

## Auto-derived environment variables

The operator sets these from the resource, so you do not repeat them in `spec.env`:

| Variable | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NODE_OPTIONS` | `spec.resources.limits.memory` | `--max-old-space-size=<75% of the memory limit in MB>` to prevent Node.js OOM kills |
| `OMNIROUTE_BASE_PATH` | `spec.basePath` | Reverse-proxy base path |
| `REDIS_URL` | `spec.redis.url` or the referenced Secret | Redis connection URL |
| `REDIS_KEY_PREFIX` | `spec.redis.keyPrefix` | Redis key namespace prefix |
| `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | `spec.encryption.existingSecret` | Database encryption key |
| `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_VERSION` | `spec.encryption.keyVersion` | Encryption key version |

## Status

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `status.conditions` | Standard conditions describing reconciliation |
| `status.readyReplicas` | Number of ready OmniRoute replicas |
| `status.observedGeneration` | Generation last processed by the operator |
| `status.phase` | High-level phase of the deployment |

Check it with:

```sh
kubectl get omniroute omniroute -n ai-platform -o yaml
```

---

---
url: /docs/omniroute-operator/local-development.md
description: >-
  Run the omniroute-operator against a local k3d cluster, build images, and run
  the controller outside Kubernetes.
---

# Local development

You need Docker >= 24, k3d >= 5.6, Go 1.27, kubectl, and Helm >= 3.12.

## Build the operator

```sh
go build -trimpath -o bin/manager ./cmd/
./bin/manager --help
```

Cross-compile the Linux binaries used by the container image:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -trimpath -o dist/linux_amd64/manager ./cmd/
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 go build -trimpath -o dist/linux_arm64/manager ./cmd/
```

## Run the tests

```sh
go test -short -timeout=120s ./...
go test -race -short -timeout=120s ./...
go vet ./...
```

Integration tests require Docker:

```sh
INTEGRATION=1 go test -v -timeout=10m -tags=integration ./tests/integration/
```

## Create a local cluster

```sh
k3d cluster create omniroute \
  --port "20128:20128@server:0" \
  --k3s-arg "--disable=traefik@server:0"

kubectl apply -k config/k3d/infrastructure   # namespaces
kubectl apply -f config/crd/bases/           # OmniRoute CRD
```

## Install the operator from source

Build the image the same way the Dockerfile expects, import it into k3d, then
install the chart with the local image:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -trimpath -o dist/linux_amd64/manager ./cmd/
docker build -t omniroute-operator:dev .
k3d image import omniroute-operator:dev -c omniroute

helm install omniroute-operator charts/omniroute-operator \
  --namespace omniroute-system \
  --set image.repository=omniroute-operator \
  --set image.tag=dev \
  --set image.pullPolicy=IfNotPresent
```

Check the controller:

```sh
kubectl get pods -n omniroute-system
kubectl get crd omniroutes.gateway.omniroute.ai
```

## Run the controller outside the cluster

Useful when you want to debug reconciliation in your IDE. Install the CRD, then
run the manager against your kubeconfig:

```sh
kubectl apply -f config/crd/bases/
./bin/manager --health-probe-bind-address=:8081
```

## Helm checks

```sh
helm lint charts/omniroute-operator --strict
helm template omniroute-operator charts/omniroute-operator \
  --namespace omniroute-system > /tmp/omniroute-operator.yaml
```

## Clean up

```sh
k3d cluster delete omniroute
```

# Documentation for coding agents

Nirantara maintains four open-source projects. The documentation below is
organised per project, and every page is also available as raw Markdown by
appending `.md` to its URL. The curated index is at [/llms.txt](/llms.txt) and
the full corpus at [/llms-full.txt](/llms-full.txt).

## Where to look

### k3sctl

Declarative K3s cluster lifecycle over SSH.

* [Overview](./docs/k3sctl/index.md)
* [Installation](./docs/k3sctl/installation.md)
* [Configuration](./docs/k3sctl/configuration.md): the `Cluster` file, hosts,
  K3s settings, and drain options.
* [Commands](./docs/k3sctl/commands.md): `apply`, `reset`, `kubeconfig`,
  `restore`, `config diff`, `config validate`, and the flags each accepts.

### mssql-mcp-go

Read-only MCP server for Microsoft SQL Server.

* [Overview](./docs/mssql-mcp-go/index.md)
* [Installation](./docs/mssql-mcp-go/installation.md)
* [Configuration](./docs/mssql-mcp-go/configuration.md): `config.yaml`,
  `SQLSERVER_*` variables, and client snippets.
* [Tools](./docs/mssql-mcp-go/tools.md)

### postgres-mcp-go

Read-only MCP server for PostgreSQL.

* [Overview](./docs/postgres-mcp-go/index.md)
* [Installation](./docs/postgres-mcp-go/installation.md)
* [Configuration](./docs/postgres-mcp-go/configuration.md): `config.yaml`,
  `POSTGRES_*` variables, and client snippets.
* [Tools](./docs/postgres-mcp-go/tools.md)

### omniroute-operator

Kubernetes operator for OmniRoute.

* [Overview](./docs/omniroute-operator/index.md)
* [Installation](./docs/omniroute-operator/installation.md)
* [OmniRoute CR](./docs/omniroute-operator/omniroute-cr.md): every field in
  `gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1`.
* [Local development](./docs/omniroute-operator/local-development.md)

## Details that are easy to get wrong

### k3sctl

1. Hosts must be Linux. `k3sctl` installs K3s and systemd units over SSH.
2. The configuration is `apiVersion: k3sctl.k3sproject.io/v1beta1`,
   `kind: Cluster`.
3. `spec.hosts[]` entries choose a `role` of `server` or `agent`. Servers are
   the default.
4. Extra YAML documents in the same file are applied after installation with
   `kubectl apply`. Separate them with `---`, and make each one a valid
   Kubernetes manifest.
5. `apply` is idempotent and only changes what drifted. `--dry-run` shows the
   plan without changing the cluster.
6. `reset` removes K3s from the hosts. It is not the same as deleting a
   namespace.

### MCP servers

1. Both servers are read-only. Mutating SQL is rejected before execution, and
   stored procedures are analysed, never run.
2. Environment variables override `config.yaml`; never assume the file wins.
3. The default transport is `stdio`, so an MCP client launches the binary rather
   than connecting to a port.
4. `mssql-mcp-go` uses `SQLSERVER_*` variables and `encrypt`/`ssl` options that
   are SQL Server specific. `postgres-mcp-go` uses `POSTGRES_*` variables and
   `ssl_mode` plus `search_path`.
5. The tool names and groups are the same across both servers, but the SQL
   dialect differs. Do not copy a T-SQL snippet into a PostgreSQL answer.

### omniroute-operator

1. The group and version are `gateway.omniroute.ai/v1alpha1`; the kind is
   `OmniRoute`.
2. `spec.replicas` is effectively capped at `1` because OmniRoute stores state
   in SQLite with a single writer.
3. Credentials come from an existing Secret with `JWT_SECRET`,
   `API_KEY_SECRET`, and `INITIAL_PASSWORD`.
4. `spec.ingress.enabled` defaults to `false`. Enable it explicitly and set
   `className`, `host`, and TLS if the instance must be public.
5. `spec.persistence.enabled` creates a PVC. Disabling it makes the instance
   ephemeral.
6. `NODE_OPTIONS` is derived from the memory limit; do not hardcode it in
   `spec.env` unless you need to override the derived value.
